title: Oracles at Delphi
subtitle: People don't disbelieve maxims, they just think they're the exception.

items.text: Oracles at Delphi

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If my pursuit of Truth will be the destruction of my beliefs?
She shakes her head repeatedly, looking more perplexed than when she checked the Manus followers' math homework.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I came for the Truth, and my faith is the Truth. Why would the Truth be destroyed by the Truth?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If it's because I did the calculation wrong, I'll go back and do it again!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: And next time, I will do better!
An answer without hesitation, causing the gatekeeper to pause for an extra moment of silence.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: What if the essence of Truth is there is no "Truth"?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hm, isn't that also a form of the "Truth"? Its non-existence is an answer in itself, is it not?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You're speaking like 210. Are you really 6?
37 has clearly run out of patience with the sophistry.
She stares at 6 in annoyance, trying to detect any sign on his face that he might be playing a joke on her.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I should be more specific. You may see it as another allegory.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: A gate stands before you. Open it, you will find the "Truth" you seek.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: But at the same time, the world as you know it will crumble. Will you still open it?
37 blinks. This time, her answer is even more clear and resolute.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Yes!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If my world changes because the Truth is revealed, doesn't that mean my previous understanding was wrong and should be corrected?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If what's behind the gate is really the Truth, why would I give up the Truth for falsehood?

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: You've passed. As a reward, I will bestow upon you this sacred ritual.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: It will bridge the gap between you and the supreme existence during communion.
A gilded scroll is presented to her.
But the winner only furrows her brows even harder.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Was that it? You didn't even ask a question that posed a real challenge!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: See, Vertin? I knew this was just a formality.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Vertin?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, 37, I think this question ...
6 interjects.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: There are some words I'd like to share with you.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Not as 6, but myself, who used to live under the name "Atticus."

items.speaker: Six
items.text: We know the story of Socrates's life, how Truth and politics are at odds with each other.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Either be wise, uninvolved, and look on; or be practical, involved, and suffer.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I hope you will remember your answer when the defining moment comes for you.
He leaves.
The game has been a disappointment. 37 frowns in frustration, but she keeps a tight grip on the scroll.
The gate in the center of the circle has swung open, but the path ahead is still shrouded in mist.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: We should go, Vertin. There's a long way ahead.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I hope the next question will be more fun.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Nothing I haven't expected so far! Just like what Mom told me.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: They're just games, like skipping rocks, kottabos, and hopscotch. I've always been good at games!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Look, there's the gate, Vertin. We're almost at the end!
37 claps her hands with satisfaction, having resolved yet another obstacle.
But her companion is much more pensive.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: What's the matter, Vertin? You've been quiet since we met 6.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But you're number 0, not 6. You have no common factor with him.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, I'm only thinking ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's the question you're going to ask? We've only got one chance.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The most important question of all, of course!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: About the "essence" of the "Emanation," right?
It was not a hard guess.
The islanders devote their lives to the study and service of "the essence." Nothing is more important than this question.
The "essence" reveals the ultimate truth that underlies all existence. Everything else is just fragments of the phenomenal world.
It might not directly solve the issue of the "Storm" immunity, but knowing its nature will certainly help with that aspect.
And it's the key to solving not just one problem, but many others.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Well, the essence of it is important.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But one day, we will eventually come to understand it. Even if we leave it alone for now, it will still be there, yes?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think so?
She seems to have something else in mind.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I can't stop thinking about Regulus. Despite being so close to the answer, she turned back in the cave, determined to earn the answer rather than receive it on a silver platter.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's like covering your ears in front of the oracles at Delphi! How typical of an irrational number.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But she was also right, wasn't she? None of the precepts forbids one from doing so.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: People like her may fall behind or get distracted along the way, learning at a slower pace. But in the end, we will all converge. It doesn't matter if some arrive sooner than others.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So, are you going to ask something else?
This time she nods.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Yes, I have come up with a better question!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: A question that will solve all our problems once and for all, and free everyone from the "Emanation"!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's not as profound as my first question, but it's an equally good one.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I will stop here then.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hm?
She turns around, eyes wide with surprise.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Vertin, are you turning back like Regulus?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But you're a 0. You're not an irrational!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, I won't go far. I will wait for you here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is your gate to open. It is your question, your answer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I will stay here and watch over you. If you encounter any danger in there, I will come to your aid at once.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But don't you also have a question to ask Apeiron?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Aren't your doubts unresolved?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. I don't need to ask anymore.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The question you're going to ask, the one that will free us all from the "Emanation,"

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: is exactly the question I want to ask, 37.
37 tilts her head curiously, but her confusion soon fades.
She quickly understands, as she does with most things in life.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I see! So you're choosing to be the one who looks on, like the third kind of men in the Olympic Games!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: A choice of insight, most appropriate for the number 0!
Without further hesitation, she turns and steps into the final gate.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: In that case, I will see you later then, Vertin!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: See you soon, 37.
Put the suitcase down, and breathe. Be ready for anything.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Will this really be the collapse of her world as she knew it, like 6 said? If that happens ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll be here to hold the umbrella for her.
TO BE CONTINUED…
